statement: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{1+x^{2}}\,dx$ and explain why the integral of the $x^{3}$ part vanishes.
solution: $\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{1+x^{2}}=\dfrac{x(x^{2}+1)}{1+x^{2}}=x$. Hence $\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{x^{3}+x}{1+x^{2}}\,dx=\int_{-1}^{1}x\,dx=0$. The $x^{3}$ term $\frac{x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}$ is an odd function integrated over a symmetric interval, so its contribution is zero.
hints: Factor the numerator to simplify the integrand.
Recognise the remaining integrand is odd.
Integrate an odd function over a symmetric interval.
